summary: Use a Chip Group to lay out a row of Chip Select filters that wraps onto new lines with even gaps.

useWhen.text: Lay out a row of Chip Select filters that wraps onto new lines with even gaps.

from.quote: Use a Chip Group to lay out a row of Chip Select filters that wraps onto new lines with even gaps.

useWhen.text: The group spaces the chips; each chip keeps its own state.

from.quote: The group spaces the chips; each chip keeps its own state.

useWhen.text: Filters that combine, such as Date and Payment methods applying together.

from.quote: Date and Payment methods apply together.

avoidWhen.text: One choice among options, such as Daily, Weekly or Monthly: people expect several chips to apply, and each is announced as its own toggle.

from.quote: People expect several to apply, and each is announced as its own toggle.

avoidWhen.text: A mutually exclusive choice: the upstream ChipGroup mdx (unpublished), as the evidence records it, points to a SegmentedControl.

avoidWhen.text: A single filter: the upstream ChipGroup mdx (unpublished), as the evidence records it, points to a ChipSelect alone.

rules.text: Name each filter in one or two words, in sentence case.

from.quote: Name each filter in one or two words, in sentence case.

accessibility.text: Name the row with accessibilityLabel, as the screen names it “Transaction filters”, so it is announced as a group.

from.quote: The screen names the row “Transaction filters”, so it is announced as a group.

accessibility.text: accessibilityLabel is the chip row's accessible name; when it is set, the row's role defaults to group.
Given an accessibility label, the row is announced as a named group; each chip is still announced as its own toggle button.

from.quote: Given an accessibility label, the row is announced as a named group; each chip is still announced as its own toggle button.

examples.purpose: Figma's three filters, from the guide's Configuration: Date, Status and Payment methods, each ChipSelect with its own icon, in one wrapping row. The screen adds each chip's active and onPress, as the next example shows.
examples.jsx:
<ChipGroup>
  <ChipSelect label="Date" icon="ic_calendar_week" />
  <ChipSelect label="Status" icon="ic_status_loading" />
  <ChipSelect label="Payment methods" icon="ic_payments" />
</ChipGroup>

from.quote: Date, Status, and Payment methods, each with its own icon.

examples.purpose: Filters above a transaction list, the guide's In context, once the screen has applied Date and Payment methods: the screen names the row “Transaction filters” and owns each chip's active and onPress; an applied chip shows its value as its label, and pressing it again clears it. The literal values and empty onPress stand for the screen's own state and picker.
examples.jsx:
<ChipGroup accessibilityLabel="Transaction filters">
  <ChipSelect label="Last 30 days" icon="ic_calendar_week" active onPress={() => {}} />
  <ChipSelect label="Status" icon="ic_status_loading" active={false} onPress={() => {}} />
  <ChipSelect label="UPI" icon="ic_payments" active onPress={() => {}} />
</ChipGroup>

from.quote: The screen owns each filter: pressing an Idle chip applies it (a picker would open here), and pressing an Active chip clears it.

props.name: children
props.description: Each chip gets maxWidth 100%, flexShrink 1, minWidth 0 and overflow hidden from the group, so a chip wider than the row shrinks to the row and wraps its label. Declared: Child elements to be rendered inside the chip group. Expects ChipSelect components. Strings and numbers are rendered as single-line text so a ReactNode child does not get dropped.

props.name: modes
props.description: Every element child gets the group's modes with its own on top (the child wins, per key). ChipSelect State can't be set from the group. Declared: Mode configuration for design tokens. These modes are passed down to all child components.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: On the web the named row gets role="group" and aria-label. Declared: Accessible name for the chip row. When set, the row's role defaults to `group`.

props.name: accessibilityRole
props.description: Accessibility role. Defaults to `group` when `accessibilityLabel` is set.

props.name: accessibilityHint
props.description: Additional accessibility hint for screen readers.

props.name: accessibilityState
props.description: Accessibility state forwarded to the row.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Child elements to be rendered inside the chip group. Expects ChipSelect components. Strings and numbers are rendered as single-line text so a ReactNode child does not get dropped.
